info.desc: Purple Rain is an album by Prince and The Revolution, the soundtrack to the film of the same name. It was released on June 25, 1984 by Warner Bros. Records. Purple Rain regularly is ranked among the best albums in rock music history. Time magazine in 1993 ranked it the 15th greatest album of all time, and it placed 18th on VH1's The Greatest Rock n Roll Albums of All Time. Rolling Stone magazine ranked it 72nd greatest album of all time and Zounds magazine 18th greatest album of all time. The album was 4th in Plásticos y Decibelios list .

podcast.body: Although released in 1984, this album became the first documented record to officially receive the Parental Advisory warning label in 1985, as it was an album conservative groups "were looking forward to" targeting. "el primer álbum del que tenemos constancia de que empezó a usarse este a etiqueta de advertencia fue en el Purple Rain de Prince, que no era de 1985, era de un año antes en 1984, pero ya era un almúal que le tenían ganas, entonces inmediatamente fue el primer almúal que le empezaron a poner las etiquetas."

podcast.body: Most of the drum sounds on Prince's album *Purple Rain* were generated using a Linn unit, thus prominently featuring the samples recorded by Art Wood. "Most of the drum sounds and princes' purple rain were a Lynn, and by extension, Art Wood."

podcast.body: This album is described as Prince's "Summary Cinematic Magnum Opus." Its lead single, "When Doves Cry," was the 1984 Song of the Summer and a top hit of one of Pop's greatest years. "It's the lead single to Prince's Summary Cinematic Magnum Opus Purple Rain and the top hit of one of Pop's greatest years."

podcast.body: This album was a "stellar" nominee for Album of the Year at the 1985 Grammy Awards, which recognized music from 1984 and late 1983. It ultimately lost to Lionel Richie's "Can't Slow Down." "among the stellar album of the year nominees were, Prince's Purple Rain, Cindy Loppers She's So Unusual, Bruce Springsteen's Born in the USA, and Tina Turner's Private Dancer."
